events.artist: Akiko Yano Trio featuring Will Lee & Chris Parker
events.subtitle: Solo debut 50th anniversary — Golden Trio
events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents Akiko Yano Trio featuring Will Lee and Chris Parker on August 21, 23, 24, 26 and 27, 2026. August 21, 24, 26 and 27 have 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM sets; August 23 has 4:30 PM and 7:30 PM sets. The venue frames the engagement around the 50th anniversary of Yano's solo debut and the return of her long-running trio with Lee and Parker, following the release of their 2025 live album recorded at Blue Note Tokyo.

recommended_listening.title: AKIKO YANO TRIO featuring Will Lee & Chris Parker Live at Blue Note Tokyo 2025.09.04

provenance.note: Exact dates, set times, lineup, 50th-anniversary framing and web-reservation path were verified on Blue Note Tokyo's event page. The recommended listening link is the exact Apple Music page for the same trio's 2025 Blue Note Tokyo live album.

en.why_it_matters: The anniversary matters because this is not a museum-piece retrospective: Yano is marking fifty years from her solo debut with the Will Lee/Chris Parker trio she calls a lifelong treasure, in the room where the same unit was documented live the previous year. Her piano language can move from jazz harmony and free rhythmic play to Japanese pop melody without losing its identity, while Lee and Parker give the music the elastic groove that makes this trio more than an accompanimental format.
en.trip_verdict: S within Greater Tokyo/Kanto. Protect a night and cross Tokyo for it: a 50th-anniversary season appearance by one of Japan's most singular pianist-composers with her established New York rhythm section is exactly the kind of context-rich date Listening Notes should preserve. Strong Tokyo-trip anchor, though not by itself a reason to cross the Pacific.

es.why_it_matters: El aniversario importa porque no es una retrospectiva de museo: Yano marca cincuenta años desde su debut solista con el trío de Will Lee y Chris Parker que ella misma describe como un tesoro de toda la vida, en la misma sala donde esa unidad quedó documentada en vivo el año pasado. Su lenguaje pianístico puede pasar de la armonía jazzística y el juego rítmico libre a la melodía del pop japonés sin perder identidad, mientras Lee y Parker le dan el groove elástico que convierte al trío en mucho más que una banda de acompañamiento.
es.trip_verdict: S dentro de Greater Tokyo/Kanto. Vale proteger una noche y cruzar Tokio por esto: una fecha de temporada por el 50 aniversario de una de las pianistas-compositoras más singulares de Japón con su sección rítmica neoyorquina establecida es exactamente el tipo de contexto que Listening Notes debe conservar. Es un ancla fuerte para un viaje a Tokio, aunque por sí sola no justifica cruzar el Pacífico.
